summary.text: Orogeny is mountain building at a convergent plate margin, where plate motion squeezes the edge until it crumples and is uplifted into ranges.
It involves both deforming existing continental crust and creating new continental crust through volcanism.
A continent riding over an ocean plate builds a noncollisional, Andean-type orogen, while continents colliding build a collisional one such as the Himalayas.

facts.label: Himalayan uplift
facts.value: Ongoing for the last 65 million years

facts.label: Laramide orogeny
facts.value: Lasted 40 million years, 75 to 35 million years ago

facts.label: Accretionary examples
facts.value: North American Cordillera and Australia's Lachlan Orogen

items.prompt: Two subduction zones look much alike, but only one has a mountain belt beside it. What most likely differs?

options.label: Only one has an ocean plate sinking
Only one sits over a mantle hotspot
Only one has plates moving apart
Only one squeezes the plate above it

items.explain: Not every subduction zone builds mountains; it happens only when subduction compresses the overriding plate.

items.prompt: An orogenic belt has frequent earthquakes and active volcanoes. What does that suggest about it?

options.label: It is old and deeply eroded
It is young, with subduction ongoing
Its plates are pulling apart
It has stopped growing for good

items.explain: Young orogenic belts, where subduction is still under way, are marked by frequent volcanic activity and earthquakes.

items.prompt: In an ancient, worn-down mountain belt, what are you likely to see exposed at the surface?

options.label: Bent rock layers and huge bodies of intrusive rock
Fresh lava flows and steaming vents
Flat, undisturbed layers of sediment
Mostly young coral reef limestone

items.explain: Old belts are deeply eroded, exposing displaced, deformed and often metamorphosed strata and vast intrusive bodies called batholiths.

items.prompt: As a mountain belt grows, a sunken basin forms just ahead of it. What mainly causes the basin?

options.label: Rivers carving out a wide valley
The ground there being pulled apart
The belt's weight bending the plate down
An old volcano collapsing inward

items.explain: A foreland basin forms mainly because the growing mountain belt loads the lithosphere and makes it flex.

items.prompt: As subduction goes on, island arcs and continental fragments get stuck onto a continent's edge. What is one big result of this?

options.label: Oceans steadily get wider
Continents grow larger
Subduction stops at once
Mountains sink back down

items.explain: Accreting arcs, fragments and oceanic material onto the margin is one of the main ways continents have grown.

items.prompt: Roughly how long can the processes that build a mountain belt take?

options.label: A few centuries
Tens of thousands of years
Tens of millions of years
Several billion years

items.explain: Orogeny can take tens of millions of years; the Laramide orogeny alone lasted 40 million years.
